content: Butz-Choquin is a French manufacturer of smoking pipes. The company was originally founded in 1858 by Jean-Baptiste Choquin, a tobacconist, and Gustave Butz. Initially based in Metz, the company operated there until 1951, when it was purchased by the Berrod-Regad company. Following this acquisition, the company was relocated to Saint-Claude, a region in Jura known for its pipe-making tradition. In 1960, Butz-Choquin began exporting its pipes internationally, earning prestigious accolades such as the Oscar of Export and the Gold Cup of the French Good Taste for its contributions to the industry. In 2002, the company was acquired by Fabien Guichon, marking a new chapter in its history. The first pipe produced by Butz-Choquin, known as the Choquin pipe, featured a distinctive design. It was a curved pipe with a flat-bottomed hearth, incorporating albatross bone and silver rings as part of its construction. Today, the company manufactures over 70 different series of pipes, showcasing a wide variety of designs and craftsmanship. Despite its long history, Butz-Choquin pipes only became widely available in the United States in 1999.
